summary: Presents a questionnaire about file systems on ARPANET hosts. A subcommittee led by Abhay Bhushan was drafting proposals for data transfer and file transfer protocols. They decided not to standardize file naming and access control for now, so users would need to know a remote system's conventions.

plainLanguage.summary: This questionnaire asks each host to explain how its file system works. The information would help network users work with remote files and support later protocol decisions.

subtitle: A questionnaire about file names, access rules and formats on network hosts.

tldr.problem: Users needed information about remote file systems because the proposed transfer protocol would not standardize local file names or access rules.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC asks hosts to document file naming, access controls, directories, commands, data representation and other important features.
tldr.outcome: Collected descriptions could help network users and inform the file transfer committee's work.

today: RFC 180 is a file system questionnaire published in June 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: Why Host File Information Is Needed
sections.content:
A Network Working Group subcommittee was preparing proposals for data transfer and file transfer. It decided that the file transfer protocol should standardize ways to request a transfer, but not file names or access-control conventions.

Users would therefore need to follow the remote host's local rules. Alex McKenzie asks hosts to provide enough information for users to understand those rules; copies of concise local documentation were acceptable.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposed transfer rules would not make every host use the same file names or access controls. Users therefore needed a guide to each host's local system.

sections.title: Information Requested
sections.content:
The questionnaire asks about pathnames and their defaults; access controls for creating and retrieving files; directory names, contents and protections; and the commands and functions a file system provides.

It also asks how data is represented and transferred, including character formats, record boundaries, file sizes and logical structure. Hosts could add details that did not fit these categories but mattered to users.
sections.plainLanguage: Hosts were asked how users name files, control access, use directories and work with file contents. They were also asked how data is represented when it is sent.

sections.title: Responses and Intended Use
sections.content:
Responses were to be sent to Alex McKenzie at BBN. The RFC says the collected information would provide a source for users and could inform future standardization work by the file transfer subcommittee.

McKenzie planned to issue another RFC summarizing responses after receiving a significant number.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites were asked to send their descriptions to BBN. The information could help both users and the group developing file transfer proposals.
